title: Where you belong
hookLine: some find their home in one tradition; some stay walking between, and Leviticus calls everyone a guest
tomorrow: what did Jesus say when two strangers asked where he lived?

lines: LAND THAT CAN'T BE SOLD FOREVER.
cards: At a party someone asks, so what are you? And they mean religion. Some people have a one-word answer.
Some say it's complicated and reach for the chips. The Torah has a line for both. In Leviticus, God gives Israel a law about land: it can't be sold forever.
And the reason, in the King James Version: "for the land is mine; for ye are strangers and sojourners with me."

teach.b: So even people settled on their own fields are called sojourners: guests. Abraham said it of himself when he asked to buy a grave for Sarah: "I am a stranger and a sojourner with you."
This is the teaching behind the Torah's land laws.
In the jubilee year, land goes back to its families, because, as the verse says, the land is God's. Belonging, here, isn't owning. That speaks to both answers at the party.
Some find their home in one tradition and stay. Some keep walking between.
By this verse, both are guests, and both can be at home. Where you are is an honest place to stand. Now gather up the stretch you just finished.
Loved: the weight that carries the rest. Missing: the rest that finishes the work. Reviewed: twice, and then done.
Version two: new stone, with the old kept beside it.
The one-breath rule: the whole thing on one foot.

teach.h: WHERE I AM IS A PLACE TO STAND.
teach.b: And ready for now, leaves and all.

how: Leviticus 25 sets the sabbatical and jubilee laws, grounded in the line that the land is God's and the people are strangers and sojourners with God. On a personal path, people name honestly where they stand now: at home in one tradition, or walking between.

s: in Leviticus, only foreigners are called strangers and sojourners
God says it to Israel on its own land: "ye are strangers and sojourners with me."
Abraham called himself a stranger and a sojourner when he asked to buy a grave for Sarah
"I am a stranger and a sojourner with you."
you can't belong anywhere until you've joined one tradition
in this verse, belonging isn't owning: everyone is a guest, settled or walking.

games.q: at a wedding, an aunt whispers that one guest doesn't really belong, since she isn't a member of the family's congregation. by Leviticus 25:23, what's a fair reply?
o: she's a guest here, and in Leviticus so is everyone: strangers and sojourners with God.
she'll belong once she officially joins the congregation.
belonging doesn't matter at a wedding anyway.
games.why: the verse is spoken to people on their own land: the land is God's, and all are guests. belonging isn't owning.

practice: Close your eyes and let one honest answer come to the question: where am I, right now? Not where you should be, or where you'll be in a year. Settled, walking, or somewhere between: rest in that answer for the sit.

carryVoice: Keep this one: where I am, a guest, and at home. That's the week, gathered up.
